titulo: State outside the model: files and git as memory
lead: In a long loop, the model's context will be compacted, reset, or swapped for a fresh session. What only existed in the conversation vanishes or comes back as a summary, mixing fact and guess. The way out: disposable session, state in files and in git, and every cycle starts by rereading. You build a cycle like this and interrupt it on purpose.
objetivo: build a disposable cycle that rereads the state from a file, does one item, verifies, and commits, and resume after an interruption without redoing anything.

aprende.t: Why the model's memory can't handle a long loop
The list of items with passes, the progress file, and the git log
Interrupt and resume without redoing or skipping
Git as undo and as the loop's history

hero_alt: Paper folders and an external drive next to a laptop, connected by thin cables that branch out.

secoes.titulo: A disposable session, a state that stays
secoes.sub: Click each step of the cycle: what it reads and what it leaves recorded.

nos.detalhe: It could be a /clear, a compaction, a fresh codex exec, Ralph calling again, or someone else taking over. The design starts from the worst case: the session remembers nothing and can be interrupted midway.

In Anthropic's long-running harness (11/26/2025), every session starts like this: where am I (pwd), what has been done (git log and the progress file), what is the next item, and a basic test before coding. The item list is JSON with the passes field; the post says the model overwrites JSON less than Markdown.

itens.t: Does not reopen an item with passes true

nos.detalhe: Picks the first pending item and does only that one. In Anthropic's post, later sessions may only change the passes field; they do not rewrite or delete items from the list.

itens.t: passes: true if the verification passed

nos.detalhe: An item only becomes passes: true if its verification passed. The line in progress says when and what the result was. If it failed, the item stays pending and the reason is recorded.

The commit is the checkpoint: if the next session drops, nothing that was verified is lost; if an item came out wrong, git revert undoes it. LOOP-R uses the same principle for process versions ("git is the promotion and rollback mechanism"; details in course 5).

secoes.volta: The session ends or drops; the next one starts by rereading the files and picks up from the first pending item.
secoes.legenda: The execucao-longa kit takes the idea to seven files (goal, plan, state, progress, failures, decisions, canal): it is lesson 1 of course 2.

rolagem_fim.titulo: Rereads the folder, not the conversation
rolagem_fim.texto: The session is disposable; the state is not. Whatever has to survive a compaction, a reset, or a model switch goes into a file and a commit before the end of the cycle.

secoes.sub: Each run is a "session" that remembers nothing: it rereads, does one item, verifies, records, and commits. No model: the action is writing a file.

blocos.conteudo:
mkdir -p ~/ensaio-loop/estado && cd ~/ensaio-loop/estado && git init -q
cat > features.json <<'EOF'
[
 {"id":"f1","descricao":"ler o CSV","passes":false},
 {"id":"f2","descricao":"contar linhas","passes":false},
 {"id":"f3","descricao":"gravar o resumo","passes":false}
]
EOF
git add -A && git commit -qm inicio

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A cycle that starts from zero every time: rereads the state from files, does ONE item, records and commits."""
import json, subprocess, sys, datetime, pathlib

estado = pathlib.Path("features.json")
itens = json.loads(estado.read_text())
pendentes = [i for i in itens if not i["passes"]]
if not pendentes:
    print("nada pendente: objetivo cumprido")
    sys.exit(0)
item = pendentes[0]
print(f"releu features.json: {len(itens) - len(pendentes)} feitos, {len(pendentes)} pendentes")
print(f"faz: {item['id']} ({item['descricao']})")
pathlib.Path(f"{item['id']}.txt").write_text(item["descricao"] + "\n")   # the "action"
item["passes"] = pathlib.Path(f"{item['id']}.txt").exists()                # the "verification"
estado.write_text(json.dumps(itens, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n")
agora = datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
with open("progress.md", "a") as f:
    f.write(f"| {agora} | {item['id']} | passes={item['passes']} |\n")
subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], check=True)
subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-qm", f"feito: {item['id']}"], check=True)
print(f"commit: feito: {item['id']}")

python3 ciclo.py
# close the terminal here, open another one and go back to the folder
cd ~/ensaio-loop/estado
python3 ciclo.py && python3 ciclo.py && python3 ciclo.py
git log --oneline

The hashes will differ on your machine; the order and the messages will not.

Swap the "action" line for a call to the agent (codex exec or claude -p) and the "verification" line for a test that actually runs. The rest (reread, one item, mark only with proof, commit) stays the same. The verification in this toy version is weak on purpose: it only checks that the file exists (level 2 on the scale from lesson 6).

secoes.titulo: Interrupt midway and watch it resume
secoes.sub: Each task is a cycle. Run it, interrupt it, and run it again: whatever already has a commit is not redone.

msg.inicio: 5 items with passes: false. Click "Run the cycles".
msg.rodando: Each cycle: rereads the list, takes the first pending item, verifies, and commits.
msg.parou: The session dropped in the middle of an item. It has no commit: it stays pending. Run it again.
msg.retoma: New session: it reread the list and git log. Whatever has a commit is not redone; the interrupted item goes back to pending.
msg.fim: Empty list: all items with passes: true and a commit.
msg.fimfalha: End of the round. One item ended up without passes because the verification failed: the reason goes into the log and it is first in the next cycle.

secoes.legenda: Illustrative simulation in the browser. The failure is intentional: an item without proof does not become passes: true.

secoes.sub: On your machine. It doesn't use up quota: there is no model in the cycle.

exercicios.titulo: E3 · The list from a job of your own
exercicios.texto: Pick a real task that takes several hours and break it into at least 5 verifiable items in a features.json, all with passes: false, in a project folder with git.
exercicios.pronto: python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('features.json'));print(len(d)>=5, any(i['passes'] for i in d))" → True False, and git log --oneline -1 -- features.json shows the commit of the list.

perguntas.p: After a compaction, the summary says "f3 done", but features.json shows f3 with passes: false and there is no commit for f3. Which one counts?
opcoes: The summary, since it is more recent
Mark f3 as true to save time
The file and git: f3 is pending
Ask the model if it remembers
perguntas.explica: The summary mixes what is confirmed with guesses. What has proof is what is in the file with a commit. Marking it without checking is exactly the shortcut the list exists to prevent.

perguntas.p: Why does Anthropic's harness post keep the list of items in JSON and not in Markdown?
opcoes: Because the model overwrites JSON less than Markdown
Because JSON is faster to read and takes up less context
Because Markdown has no fields to mark what passed
Because Claude Code only reads state files in JSON
perguntas.explica: That is the reason given in the post itself: with JSON the model tends to just change the passes field, instead of rewriting the list. Later sessions can only change that field.

perguntas.p: What is the advantage of one commit per item instead of one commit at the end?
opcoes: None, it just clutters the history
The model reads small commits better
Each verified item becomes a resume point and can be undone on its own
perguntas.explica: If the session drops, what was verified is saved; if an item came out wrong, git revert undoes only that one. A single commit at the end loses everything in a crash and mixes right with wrong.

perguntas.p: In the simulation, the session dropped in the middle of an item. What happens to that item on resume?
opcoes: It's discarded and dropped from the item list
It goes to failed and requires human review
It goes back to pending, because it has no commit
It's marked as done, since it had already started
perguntas.explica: Without verification and without a commit, there is no proof it finished: it goes back to pending and is redone. What already has a commit is not redone.

itens.texto: Design for the worst case: the next session remembers nothing and may drop in the middle.
The list with passes, the progress file, and git log say where you stopped; the conversation summary does not.

itens.t: One item, one proof, one commit
itens.texto: passes only becomes true with verification, and each verified item becomes a resume point.
